title: Bread Proofing Temperature Drift
dataSources: Sourdough monitor (`sourdough:reading`), BBQ/sous-vide probes (`bbq:probe`), fridge/freezer/oven temperature (`kitchen:appliance`), espresso shots (`espresso:shot`), pantry inventory (`pantry:item`), kombucha brew (`kombucha:reading`).
app: ESP32/ESPHome kitchen sensors (sourdough rise, BBQ/sous-vide probes, fridge/freezer temperature), espresso-shot logs, and pantry inventory via MQTT and Splunk HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=sourdough:reading
| bin _time span=1h
| stats avg(temp_c) as avg_temp, stdev(temp_c) as temp_sd by batch_id _time
| where avg_temp<23 OR avg_temp>28 OR temp_sd>1.5
| sort - temp_sd
description: Checks whether the proofing environment stayed in the warm, stable range your dough expects instead of swinging wildly with the kitchen.
value: Fermentation quality depends heavily on temperature consistency; a drift alert turns better bread into a repeatable process rather than a lucky one.
implementation: Forward proofing-box or kitchen-sensor temperature into Splunk; review batches with unstable or off-target temperature windows.
visualization: Hourly trend of proofing temperature with variance markers.
grandmaExplanation: It logs when the dough's temperature has drifted outside the steady range that helps it rise well.
